newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo shares hit by rights issue.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo shares hit by rights issue.

text.p: Shares in British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc fell on Wednesday after the oil exploration company announced a two-for-nine rights issue to raise a net 167.3 million stg.
The shares were down 32-1/2p at 13.80 stg by 0752 GMT.
"The rights issue has taken the wind out of the shares," one market-maker said.
British-Borneo said it had an exciting exploration and development programme and estimated that capital expenditure up to the end of the year 2000 was likely to exceed 500 million stg.
It said it had agreed to buy Conoco's 50-percent interest in blocks in the Gulf of Mexico.
Tony Alves, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite, said he expected the shares to firm after the initial negative impact of the rights issue.
"It's a very ambitious company and they've expanded their portfolio with this new acquisition," Alves said.
"They have a very heavy schedule of capital expenditure and exploration going forward in the next few years, so it was always on the cards that they would need to expand their equity base," he said.
"Once people have digested the rights issue I think today's news will probably be seen as very positive. I still think there is a lot of mileage in the stock."
Alves said the company's announcement that its full-year dividend would remain at 8.25p per share this year was no surprise.
"One wouldn't expect a company with such an attractive range of projects in which to invest their cashflow to increase the income to the shareholder at the moment," he said.
